Sol.386.(c) Captivity the state of being confined or imprisoned. Freedom -the state of being free, without restrictions. Liberty the condition of being free from oppressive restrictions. Surrendered -to give up control or submit. Carefree -free from worries or responsibilities.
Sol.387.(c) Boldness the willingness to take risks or act with confidence. Cowardice -lack of bravery or fearfulness. Vigourphysical strength or good health. Hazard a danger or risk. Abundance -a large quantity of something.
Sol.388.(a) Unpredictable -not consistent or expected. Consistent  acting or done in the same way over time. Appreciative -showing gratitude or recognition. Enthusiastic -showing  excitement  or strong interest. Standard -a level of quality or requirement.

items.text:
Sol.389.(a) Clear  easy to understand. Enigmatic -mysterious, puzzling, or difficult to understand. Mysterious difficult or impossible to explain or understand. Instigating provoking or inciting action. Thrilling -causing excitement or emotion.
Sol.390.(a)  Lazy  unwilling  to  work  or use effort. Diligent showing careful and persistent effort or hard work. Persistent continuing firmly in a course of action despite difficulty. Squander -to waste resources or opportunities. Frazzle to exhaust or wear out.
Sol.391.(d) Energetic -showing or involving great activity or vitality. Languid lacking energy or enthusiasm.
Antonyms
Exceptional unusual or extraordinary. Lazy unwilling to work or use effort. Loyal -showing firm and constant support or allegiance.
Sol.392.(d) Ordinary normal or usual. Quaint -attractively unusual or old-fashioned. Distinct clearly different or unique. Ridiculous -deserving or inviting mockery. Brisk quick or energetic.

items.text:
Sol.397.(a)  Calm  a  state  of  peace  or tranquility. Hysterics an uncontrollable outburst of emotion, often laughter or crying. Insanity a state of mental instability. Cray  informal slang for crazy or erratic behavior. Aghast filled with shock or horror.
Sol.398.(d)  Encouraged  given support, confidence, or hope. Dishearten to cause someone to lose hope or confidence. Inspired -filled  with  the  urge  to  do something creative or admirable. Pieces individual parts of a whole. Greatest -of the highest quality or importance.
Sol.399.(a) Cowardsomeone who lacks the courage to face danger or difficulty. Brave -showing courage or facing danger without fear. Courageous having or showing bravery in challenging situations. Shallow lacking depth or seriousness. Foolish -lacking good sense or judgment.
Sol.400.(d)  Relish  to  enjoy  or  to  take great pleasure in something. Rue to feel regret for something. Distress  state  of  extreme  anxiety  or pain. Guilt -feeling of regret for doing something wrong or harmful. Loss -state of  losing  something  or someone.

items.text:
Sol.401.(d) Wasteful using resources in a  way  that  leads to unnecessary loss or expense. Frugal  careful  when  using  money  or food. Conventional -following normal or traditional ways of doing things. Cooperative  willing  to  help  and  work with others. Dynamic full of energy.
Sol.402.(d) Conservative -favoring traditional values and cautious  about change. Liberal open to new ideas and changes. Central  being  the  most important part of something. Ineffectual not producing the desired result. Hysterical -showing uncontrolled emotions, such as extreme laughter.
Sol.403.(c)  Obedient  willing to comply with an order or request. Troublesome -causing difficulty or annoyance. Soulful expressing deep emotion, often conveying  sincerity,  passion,  or a strong feeling. Planless having no plan or aim. Curious  eager  to  learn  or  know  more about something.
Sol.404.(c) Vacant available to be used. Occupied being used by someone. Overflowed to flow over the edges of a container.
